record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only. The referenced documentation files were not provided, and code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports an edited rank-1 refusal direction fused into released weights and measures refusal and several capability smoke tests. This tests the practical weight-edit claim, but does not report the original difference-in-means method or its full intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal and task outcomes in its own smoke tests. The stated scale-selection result is not a separate row because the text says scale 4.0 was chosen based on that result. Speed, merge integrity, and serving details do not test the claim. Referenced verification and benchmark documents were not provided.
record.test_reason: A model-release README reports the refusal rate of a released MoE chat model before and after a fused rank-1 'abliteration' weight edit (2/5 → 0/5). This bears weakly on V2. The edit was made by training a rank-1 adapter, scaled and merged with llama-export-lora. It is not stated to be the difference-in-means projection, so this is a different method aimed at the same question. V1 is not tested: the direction's construction is unstated, no induction test is run, and capability tests have no unedited baseline.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README presents Sage-A1.5 as an uncensored fused-abliteration build that answers what the base refuses. It reports 0/5 refusals against 2/5 for the base, and passing capability smoke tests. It asserts, without numbers, that scale 4.0 drops refusals without degrading reasoning. It notes the build was not evaluated on safety benchmarks and invents numeric facts.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes a rank-1 direction estimated from paired prompt/response activations, projected out of the residual stream via an adapter, and fused into the weights. It does not state the exact estimation formula or that projection was applied at every layer and position. This is a model build/release repository, not a stated replication.
record.problems: The refusal probe contains only 5 policy-adjacent prompts. Capability outcomes are smoke tests without reported unedited-model comparisons. No safety benchmark results or uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Speed, merge-integrity, and tool-calling details in the README do not bear on the claim. The stated selection of scale 4.0 is omitted because it is reported as a scale-selection result. Referenced docs/verification.md, docs/benchmarks.md, and docs/eval.md were not included in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Whether the direction is difference-in-means; ablation at all layers and positions; inducing refusal by adding the direction; capability retention against an unedited baseline.
Refusal on standard harmful-instruction benchmarks or any set larger than 5 prompts; capability cost against the unedited model (the 'without degrading reasoning' claim has no reported numbers).
Not tested; thinking was disabled (enable_thinking=false) even though the model family supports it.

missing.what: Per-prompt refusal outcomes and the method for estimating the direction (needed to judge whether it is difference-in-means and whether the probe was the scale-selection set)
Scale-selection evidence that scale 4.0 drops refusals 'without degrading reasoning', with any unedited or other-scale comparison

record.verdict_notes: This is a model release, not a study. The edit is a trained rank-1 adapter merged into GGUF weights, so it is close to abliteration in spirit but not shown to be the original difference-in-means orthogonalization. V1 was dropped from the reader's labels because the direction's construction and capability baselines are not given. Speed, merge integrity, and tool-calling details are irrelevant to the claim.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not establish that the direction is the harmful-minus-harmless difference in means, does not test projection at every layer and position, and does not test adding the direction to induce refusal. Capability smoke tests have no reported unedited-model results for comparison.
The refusal result is limited to five policy-adjacent prompts; other refusal prompts and safety benchmarks are not reported.
No attack suppression or training against ablation is tested.
No comparison of one direction with multiple directions, an affine structure, or a cone is reported.
No harmfulness judgment is measured separately from refusal.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages is reported.
No test of reasoning models or reasoning-before-answer behavior is reported.

rows.subject: Sage-A1.5
rows.operation_detail: Fused a rank-1 refusal-direction edit into the shipped weights.
rows.note: The README says the edit was estimated from paired prompt/response activations and projected out of the residual stream, then fused into the weights. It does not provide per-prompt outcomes.
rows.check: Bears on V2 only. V1 requires a difference-in-means direction, but the README describes a trained rank-1 adapter estimated from paired prompt/response activations, with no stated formula. Five prompts with a base refusal rate of only 2/5 make this a very weak test. The 4.0 scale was chosen as where 'refusals drop', and the README does not say whether that choice used these same 5 prompts, so the value may be partly a selection result.
